_comment: Backfill for r20261006-0053 (one blast), published with: make_bundle.py --run r20261006-0053 --compare r20260929-1647 --compare-blast-index 0 --backfill benchmark/report/backfill/2026-10-06-mmap-subsecond.json. Sources: benchmark/README.md, config.sh and consensus-parameters.yaml at harness f186c4c, the run manifest, the generators' results and logs, the combined per-second chain series, the saved node logs, and telcoin-network commit 964087e02.
title: Sub-second consensus and the mmap pack-file backend on the c3 Hyperdisk fleet
summary: We re-ran the 29 September benchmark on the same fleet shape, ten c3-highcpu-8 validators with Hyperdisk Balanced disks, with a telcoin-network build that has sub-second consensus timestamps active from genesis and the mmap pack-file storage backend, and with the consensus delays cut from 3 s, 1 s and 1 s to a 500 ms maximum header delay, a 250 ms minimum header delay and a 250 ms maximum batch delay. The harness killed validator-05 at 02:09:55 UTC, 42 seconds before its epoch was due to close, and about 20 seconds later the other nine validators stopped committing: no transaction landed for 301 seconds, from 02:10:15 to 02:15:16 UTC, and the chain moved again only after validator-05 was restarted at 02:15:00 and its first header was certified. Against the 29 September run (r20260929-1647), where a mid-epoch kill of the same validator left the other nine running, average chain throughput with all ten load generators running fell 21%, from 4,177 to 3,320 tx/s; the stall sits inside that window, and with its 301 seconds left out the average is 3,983 tx/s, 5% lower. The median time for a transaction to land over the whole blast fell from 4.0 s to 3.2 s while the 95th percentile rose from 14.4 s to 26.1 s; the stall and the two under-funded generators (03 and 04) sit inside that latency measurement. The restarted validator was proposing again 16 seconds after its restart, but because the chain had stalled it had only about 20 seconds of commits to catch up on, so this run says nothing about the 25-minute catch-up seen on 29 September. The logs show the stall sequence but not why the nine running validators could not proceed without the tenth.

evidence_detail: Commit 964087e02 is the head of the public integration branch devnet-bench-10-5-2026, made for this benchmark, whose seven merge commits bring in fix/consensus-marker-and-import-guard, fix/1443-batch-cache-prune, fix/epoch-restart-recovery, feat/1564-probe-every-sync-peer, fix/1562-consensus-output-backpressure, fix/1565-epoch-complete-range-miss and fix/1563-epoch-pack-request-queue.

load.placement: one blaster per validator, in that validator's zone, sending only to it

methodology: Before creating anything, the harness resolved the node image tag adiri:mmap-subsecond-10-5-2026 to its registry digest and pinned the run to that digest. It ran the pinned image to confirm that it reports telcoin-network 0.1.0 built from commit 964087e02, has the sub-second timestamp fork active from genesis and contains the log messages later checks rely on, and it recorded the committed consensus parameters file and its three delays.
Preflight checked access, tools, quotas and a clean genesis directory, and confirmed the load-generator image built from tn-transaction-generator commit 3644adc.

The harness created ten validators and one observer on c3-highcpu-8 (8 vCPU, 16 GB), each with a 100 GB Hyperdisk Balanced boot disk provisioned at 20,000 IOPS and 800 MiB/s, two validators in each of five regions, and opened the consensus ports between the nodes only.
It generated validator keys and built genesis for a separate benchmark chain (chain id 32286, 20-minute epochs).

It finalized each node's configuration with the committed benchmark consensus parameters: maximum header delay 500 ms, minimum header delay 250 ms and maximum batch delay 250 ms, with every other key as in the devnet defaults. The file sets no vote timeout, so the node's built-in 5 s applied. It then started the chain.
It relabelled each node's metrics agent so that every sample from these nodes is recorded under the benchmark network, never the live devnet.

It restarted the nodes one at a time with RPC open on the internal network, waiting after each until the node answered with the benchmark chain id and consensus rounds were advancing. Each node's boot lines had to show the pinned commit, the three consensus delays and the fork schedule recorded at the gate, and all eleven did. An on-node sampler was then started on each node.

A health gate confirmed that all eleven nodes reported to Prometheus under the benchmark network with consensus rounds rising, and a read of the ConsensusRegistry through an RPC tunnel confirmed the 1,200 s epoch duration.
It deployed the devnet contract set that the mixed workload calls.

A one-off funder VM funded 600 sender accounts for each of ten e2-standard-2 load generators, one per validator in that validator's zone and sending only to it, and the generators then started together.
Each generator ran 120 s of warm-up, 2,400 s of mixed load across 13 transaction types and 180 s of cool-down.

The chaos schedule was timed to the chain's epochs. Before the load generators were created, the harness read the ConsensusRegistry at a pinned block to locate the epoch boundaries and chose the first epoch close at least 600 s into the planned mixed phase, 02:10:37 UTC. It set validator-05's container to be killed with SIGKILL 59 s before that close and held down, the node to be restarted 300 s after the kill, and the observer's node to be restarted 300 s after that. The run had one blast and no injected network delay.

Afterwards the harness collected each generator's results and the on-node sampler files, merged the generator results with aggregate.py, derived the sizing figures with derive-sizing.py, and pulled 60-second machine metrics from Cloud Monitoring and 15-second node metrics from Prometheus.

Teardown began at 02:54 UTC. It saved every node's logs, sampler files and service journal, then deleted the fleet, which was gone by 03:06 UTC. The publishing pipeline then read each node's logged commit, consensus delays, vote timeout and fork schedule back from those logs.
caveats: The all-generators window (02:00:09 to 02:30:16 UTC, 1,807 s) contains the 301-second stall. From 02:10:17 all nine running validators stayed at consensus round 1787 of epoch 2 and re-proposed their headers every 500 ms. Six of them had their round-1787 headers certified; validators 03, 04 and 10 logged repeated failures to collect votes for theirs. Headers in this run named at least seven parent certificates from the round before, and the logged quorum was seven of ten. The round moved on at 02:15:17 UTC, less than a second after validator-05's own round-1787 header was certified. Our working hypothesis is that the next round needed seven certificates and only six existed until validator-05 returned. The logs do not show why three of the nine running validators could not collect votes, so the cause of the stall is not established.

Epoch 2 was due to close at 02:10:37 UTC. The nodes detected that boundary only at the first commit after the stall, at 02:15:17, and epoch 3 started at 02:15:22, so every later epoch boundary moved by about 4 minutes 40 seconds (the epoch-3 boundary fell at 02:35:16 instead of 02:30:37). Apart from the block that closed epoch 2, at 02:15:16, no block was produced from 02:10:15 until 02:15:36.

Eight of the ten load generators, all but those for validators 05 and 06, stopped waiting for their setup transactions at the 600-second preamble limit with between 24 and 600 of their 600 senders still missing a setup step, and began their mixed phase about ten minutes late, at about 02:00 UTC. Generators 05 and 06 saw every setup transaction land within 8 s and ran from 01:50:16 to 02:30:16. The merged mixed window, 01:50:16 to 02:40:09 UTC (2,993 s), therefore has about ten minutes at each end with only two or eight generators running; it averages 3,329 tx/s. On 29 September three generators started late.

The offered load was uneven. Generators 03 and 04 sent about 120,000 transactions each over the blast, against about 850,000 to 2.5 million for the other eight. Generator 04 had no sender whose setup completed and sent no stablecoin transfers, Uniswap transactions or WTEL unwraps. Their transactions also waited longest: median time to land 108.5 s for generator 03 and 76.9 s for generator 04 (95th percentile 577.7 s and 663.0 s), against 6 to 16 s at the 95th percentile for the other seven generators; these waits are part of the whole-blast p95 of 26.1 s.

Validator-05 never reported catch-up mode. Its log shows it recovered its storage, booted directly as an active voting validator at 02:15:15 UTC and proposed its first header at 02:15:16, 16 s after the restart. The rejoin time in the recovery table, 02:15:28, is the first 15-second Prometheus sample after the restart, and the catch-up time is empty because no demotion was recorded.

The schedule set the kill for 02:09:38 UTC and the restart for 02:14:38. The kill ran at 02:09:55, 42 s before the boundary rather than 59 s, the restart at 02:15:00 (305 s later) and the observer restart at 02:20:04. The observer was following the chain again by 02:20:09, and chain throughput in the two minutes after its restart, 3,778 tx/s, was in line with the two minutes before, 3,695 tx/s.

The kill was timed differently in the two runs. On 29 September validator-05 was killed 15 minutes into the mixed phase, wherever that fell in the epoch, and the other nine validators kept the chain running; here the kill landed 42 s before an epoch was due to close and the chain stopped until the node returned. Recovery figures from the two runs are not like for like, and one run cannot say whether the stall comes from the kill's timing within the epoch, from the new build or delays, or from something else.

The comparison run, r20260929-1647, used the devnet consensus timing (3 s maximum header delay, 1 s minimum header delay, 1 s maximum batch delay, read from its node logs; its page publishes no consensus block) and the image built from main at e85bd7a3f. Both the node build and the consensus timing changed between the runs, so no difference in throughput or latency can be assigned to either one alone.

The node build is commit 964087e02, the head of the integration branch devnet-bench-10-5-2026, made for this benchmark, that merges seven fix and feature branches. It is not a tagged release, and the effect of any one of those branches cannot be separated from the rest.

The published vote timeout, 5,000 ms, is the node's built-in default, since the parameters file does not set one; this build logs it at startup. The 29 September build did not log a vote timeout, so whether it differed between the two runs is not recorded.
This is the first run of this image on this fleet, and each configuration has been run once, so run-to-run variation is not measured and the stall has been seen once.
The tag adiri:mmap-subsecond-10-5-2026 is mutable. The harness resolved it to digest sha256:61fe433a… before any node was created, and every node ran that digest.
